children: Tech Mahindra is expected to report flattish to modest margin expansion in the September-ending quarter, offsetting the impact of wage hikes through ongoing cost-efficiency initiatives such as Project Fortius.
Analysts at Nuvama Research and JM Financial expect margin expansion of 10-20 basis points, even as business investments and wage hikes are estimated to exert a 70-80 bps drag on margins.

“Tech Mahindra is likely to report over 1.6 per cent CC (constant-currency) QoQ growth and over 1.5 per cent QoQ growth in USD terms, led by telecom. This is despite an approximately 1.3 per cent headwind, which should be mitigated by the Orange deal. We expect management to maintain its 15 per cent FY27 margin guidance,” said Nuvama in a research note.

On the revenue front, analysts expect 1.2-1.7 per cent sequential growth in constant-currency terms, driven largely by the retail and healthcare verticals, along with contributions from the Orange deal. The company is also benefiting from the ramp-up of strong deal wins from previous quarters, partly offset by a decline in Pininfarina revenues following the completion of a large programme in Q1.

“The Avant Techno Solutions acquisition will contribute two months of revenue. Deal momentum should remain healthy. BFSI, manufacturing, communications and healthcare are expected to remain the key growth areas,” said Motilal Oswal Financial Services.

Meanwhile, Kotak Institutional Equities noted that the rupee’s depreciation of 0.8 per cent sequentially and 8.4 per cent annually may not immediately boost net profit for many IT companies due to cash-flow hedging practices.
“Tech Mahindra is likely to report meaningful forex losses. We expect a forex loss of $25 million for the quarter,” it said.
Deal wins are expected to remain in the $800 million to $1 billion range during the quarter.

“The turnaround is taking hold, with growth returning to around 6 per cent annually, backed by strong bookings and revenue visibility. Project Helix is helping the company transition from Fortius-led efficiency gains to AI-led growth, supported by strong execution under CEO Mohit Joshi,” said Anand Rathi.

Analysts advise investors to closely monitor management commentary on margin expansion versus reinvestment to accelerate revenue growth, the longer-term outlook for the telecom and manufacturing verticals following their expected revival in FY27 driven by two large deal ramp-ups, pricing pressures in renewal contracts, and increasing client demands for productivity gains..

title: Tech Mahindra Q2 preview: Margins seen holding up despite wage hike impact
